newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium breathes relief as swaps "loss" lessens.
newsitem.headline: Belgium breathes relief as swaps "loss" lessens.

text.p: The maximum potential loss faced by Belgium on a series of botched derivative operations on its debt was presently under 20 billion Belgian francs, down from 38 billion francs last year, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Thursday.

The maximum potential impact on Belgium's deficit was negligible, he added. "It's something like two billion francs in interest payments (on the loss) over 12 years," Maystadt told a news conference to present the Treasury's annual debt report.

The recovery in the still outstanding positions, some of which run to 2002, was due to a recovery in European foreign exchange rates to nearer pre-1992 ERM crisis levels and the recent rise in the U.S. and Canadian dollars, he said.

Maystadt was grilled last year when it emerged the Treasury faced huge potential losses arising from foreign exchange and currency swaps and associated option operations done in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
